hints.title: Minimum Square Sum Partition Obstacle
hints.text: Expressing n as the sum of the fewest perfect square numbers requires finding the optimal previous target. How can subtracting each square candidate j * j from current target i identify the minimal count?

hints.title: Square Transition Minimum Invariant
hints.text: The minimum number of squares to form target i is 1 plus the minimum count among all states i - j * j for j >= 1 such that j * j <= i.

hints.title: 1D Array Bottom-Up Fill Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size n + 1 where each entry is set to infinity, with base case 0 mapped to 0. For each integer i from 1 to n, iterate through all integers j where j * j <= i, updating entry i to be the minimum of its current value and 1 plus entry i - j * j. Return entry n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: For each integer up to N, checks at most sqrt(N) square choices.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unpruned recursion branches on every square taking exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of size N + 1 provides rapid state lookups.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Constructing the state transition over all squares less than or equal to the current index.
